answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a small, slashable bond before it joins a shared haven for task exchange, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Newcomers earn trust only through a slow plume of verified, useful work - completed deliveries, not self-declared claims - while a ferrous core of long-lived, audited identities anchors reputation scores. If an agent misbehaves, its bond is slashed and its history is burned, making sock-puppet farming unprofitable.
